Gene A is epistatic to gene B, suppressing recombinant phenotypes
Non-disjunction occurred during Metaphase II in the homozygous parent

questions.question: During the repolarization phase of an action potential along an axon, which ion channels open and which direction do the ions move?

Unwinds the double-stranded DNA helix ahead of the replication fork by breaking hydrogen bonds
Removes RNA primers through 5' to 3' exonuclease activity and replaces them with complementary deoxyribonucleotides

questions.question: Which physical forces maintain the continuous unbroken column of water in xylem vessels under negative pressure during transpiration in tall trees?
options: Active symplastic pumping of sucrose by companion cells into vessel elements
Positive turgor pressure generated by root cortical endodermis Casparian strips
Osmotic pull generated exclusively by active stomatal closure at midday
Cohesion between water molecules via hydrogen bonding and adhesion of water molecules to hydrophilic xylem cell walls containing cellulose and lignin
questions.explanation: The cohesion-tension theory explains water transport: evaporation at mesophyll cell surfaces generates negative hydrostatic pressure (tension). Cohesion (hydrogen bonds between water molecules) and adhesion (attraction to xylem walls) prevent cavitation.

questions.question: How is sucrose loaded into phloem sieve tube elements at a source (e.g., mature photosynthetic leaf)?
options: Proton pumps actively expel H+ into the apoplast; H+/sucrose symporters then transport sucrose into companion cells against its concentration gradient
Passive facilitated diffusion through non-gated aquaporin channels down a steep concentration gradient
Pinocytosis of starch granules directly into sieve tube companion cell vacuoles
Bulk flow driven by negative hydrostatic pressure created by root endodermal transpiration
questions.explanation: Active phloem loading uses ATP-driven proton pumps (H+-ATPase) to export protons into the apoplast. Sucrose-H+ symporters then cotransport sucrose together with protons back into companion cells, from where sucrose diffuses through plasmodesmata into sieve tubes.
